pages: A boundary hedge runs dead straight across two fields at Little Netherby, hawthorn and blackthorn woven into one flat green wall that bends for nobody. Middle distance: the ditch between the fields and its single hatch, weathered grey oak, standing propped open. Background: beans on one side, barley on the other, the wood at the corner beyond. Low early sun lying along the hedge top.

Foreground: a boy on a ditch bank, counting the weeks off the fingers of his left hand. Middle: the gap in the hedge and a blackbird's bare crook, the hatch beyond it. Background: two flat fields under a wide pale sky, late spring afternoon. Light: soft slanting light, long shadow on the bank.

Two blackthorn cuttings stand in a trampled gap in a hedge at the corner of a wood, bare March earth around them. Middle distance: Pell Halsey, nine, dark brown hair, a brown corduroy jacket, kneeling in the gap with a third cutting pressed into the soil. Background: the thorn tangle, the wood edge. One warm light, long soft shadows.

Mabel Dunn, sixty, grey hair scraped back, in an ochre smock and a blue apron, squats in the gap with her work-worn hand held flat above two thorn stems, not touching them. Middle distance: the two cuttings and her billhook in the grass, dark earth on her fingers. Background: the long straight boundary hedge and the ditch bank behind. Cool clear March morning light.

Ruben Halsey, fifty, sun-blackened and greying at the temple, a brown waistcoat over a bleached shirt, stands on the ditch bank with cut nettles at his boots. Middle distance: a thorn tree six feet high in the hedge gap, a leaning fence post. Background: rough grass, nettles, the far field. One warm light, long soft shadows.

Ruben Halsey, fifty, greying at the temple, in a heavy grey coat with the collar turned up, stands in his own farmyard with one hand lifted, speaking. Middle distance: a five-barred gate standing open on its hinge, its bar laid down in the grass. Background: low farm sheds and bare beaten yard, evening. Low red sun, long shadow across the yard.

Pell Halsey, nine, dark brown hair, in a grey-green wool coat, stands at a five-barred farm gate with one hand flat on the top rail, looking up, lips moving. Middle distance: the gate and its dropped bar, a stubble field running to the hedge. Background: the east field and the blackthorn boundary line under a pale afternoon sky. Flat light, one small shadow.

Wil Cobb, sixty, heavy brow, white stubble, in a dark green overcoat, stands in the gap with his hands at his sides, facing the thorn tree. Middle distance: the thorn grown right across the gap, the ditch hatch standing open behind it. Background: the boundary hedge running dead straight, the evening sky going cold. Last low light on the coat, blue shade behind.

Pell Halsey, nine, dark brown hair, in a white shirt with the sleeves pushed up, holds a small dark fruit on his fingertips, looking at it. Middle distance: a low branch thick with dark fruit, one fallen fruit in the grass. Background: the thorn in the gap at night, the hedge a black wall beyond. Warm low light rakes the fruit, deep blue dark behind.

Wil Cobb, sixty, heavy brow, in a slate-blue coat, stands in the gap with his arms folded, looking down at the thorn tree. Middle distance: the tree in leaf with a moss-lined nest low in its crook, the cut hedge ends either side. Background: the gap opening on two green fields, spring. Bright clean morning light, cool blue shade behind.
